title: Most conservative states depend more on federal aid, data show
text: A new analysis by the Tax Foundation, a nonpartisan research group devoted to educating taxpayers, shows that some of the most conservative states in the nation are the most dependent on the federal government. This may appear inconsistent with Republicans' opposition to the federal government. While some conservative states are opposed to it, the most Republican states, particularly in the Bible Belt in the south, rely on federal funding far more than the most liberal states in the nation, which is ironic. According to the data, five of the ten most conservative states in the country are among the top 10 (out of 50) that are most reliant on the federal government. The figures are calculated as the share of state government revenue that comes from the federal government, as opposed to sources within the state. Each state is assigned a percentage, shown on a map. Federal funding can include Medicaid payments, education funding, infrastructure financing and grants. Mississippi ranks No. 1 in both categories; it is the most conservative state and the most dependent. That is one example. Each state would likely shift toward the Democratic Party quickly if Republicans implemented most of their economic policies affecting the poor. The data show that some of the most conservative states in the country would barely be able to function without the federal government. California is the most populous state by a wide margin and is considered one of the top six most liberal states, the kind that passes the progressive reforms conservatives say they oppose. Its ranking differs from that of the conservative states.

title: Fury on the slopes: tainted Russians still racing as athletes revolt!
text: They cheated – so why are they still competing? Many of the world’s winter athletes, gearing up for the season’s championship events, are fed up with how sports officials have handled the Russian doping scandal, and they want to know why implicated Russian Olympians keep turning up at the starting line. The anger is boiling over. Hundreds of athletes from dozens of nations have signed petitions, threatened to boycott major events and demanded that sports authorities act on evidence that the urine samples of dozens of Russian athletes were tampered with to hide widespread doping at the last Winter Olympics, in Sochi, Russia, in 2014. And yet? Russian athletes implicated in the Sochi cheating have kept competing, and not one has been disqualified by the International Olympic Committee, as officials press on with inquiries of their own. “We will not sacrifice a full and thorough investigation that will be legally scrutinized simply to speed up the process,” Mark Adams, a spokesman for the Olympic committee, said Tuesday. Russia’s doping schemes have forced Olympic officials to widen their retesting of summer Olympians – which has already led to sanctions against dozens of athletes – but that scrutiny has barely touched winter athletes so far. The Association of International Olympic Winter Sports Federations pointed to four major competitions pulled out of Russia for the season after an outcry from athletes, including the skiing World Cup finals and the bobsled and skeleton world championships. But accused Russian athletes are still in those competitions, the organization said, because of “the presumption of innocence, the right to be heard and due process.” The pressure is mounting. Answering a petition signed by more than 150 athletes, global officials for biathlon will meet in Austria on Wednesday, ahead of that sport’s world championships, to discuss the doping scandal and broader disciplinary policy.

title: ABC cancels Tim Allen's “Last Man Standing” despite high ratings; viewers object
text: Tim Allen's sitcom Last Man Standing has ended. ABC announced that it has canceled the show after six seasons. “This was a scheduling decision,” Jori Arancio, senior vice president of ABC Entertainment and ABC Studios, wrote in an email to Fox News on Friday. According to Deadline, ABC and its production partner for the show, 20th Century Fox TV, typically negotiate licensing fees before each season, but the network decided to end the show. A representative for 20th Century Fox TV said that cancellation decisions are made by ABC. In December 2016, Tim Allen addressed microaggressions in an episode of the ABC sitcom. In an installment titled Precious Snowflake, Allen, who plays conservative family man Mike Baxter, argued with his daughter Mandy over the issue on college campuses. Many fans were surprised by the cancellation given the show's high ratings. Deadline reports that the sitcom was the network's second-highest-rated comedy this season, with an average of 8.1 million viewers, just behind Modern Family, which averaged 8.7 million viewers and was recently renewed for two more seasons. It was also ABC's third most-watched scripted series, behind Grey's Anatomy and Modern Family. Viewers objected on social media. Linda Smith wrote on May 12, 2017: “I am so upset that ABC has decided to cancel Last Man Standing because Tim Allen is conservative. It's funny.” Mary Popish wrote on May 11, 2017: “Wow ABC good job showing free speech by ending a conservative tv show cause you don't agree with it. best show!” Another viewer wrote that they were infuriated that ABC is cancelling the show despite high ratings and viewership and that they could find entertainment on other networks.

title: Stocks and debt: market outlook under a Trump presidency
text: On election night, as political analysts considered the possibility of a Trump presidency, Dow Jones futures fell more than 800 points and Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 fell more than 6.1%. Investors went to sleep concerned about protectionism (Smoot-Hawley Trade Tariffs 2.0) and the fiscal problems a Trump presidency might bring. By the start of trading on November 9th, however, Dow futures had recovered most of their losses, and the previously weak equity markets soon turned sharply positive. Markets concluded that the country may have elected a pro-growth president alongside a compliant Republican Congress. For Wall Street, it was once again “Morning in America.” However, before investors move their savings into an S&P 500 ETF and become complacent, it is necessary to explain why the markets have moved ahead of fundamentals and where the risks lie. The earnings recovery for equities had depended on a falling USD and a rebound in oil prices. Most importantly, markets had relied on the Fed’s provision of artificially low interest rates for the foreseeable future. However, oil prices have fallen from over $51 a barrel a month ago to $45 today. The dollar index has risen from 98.61 before the election to over 101, a fourteen-year high, and long-term interest rates are rising sharply. Interest rates on the 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 3.95%, up from 3.77% the previous week, the highest level since January of this year. Rates on the 15-year fixed-rate and five-year adjustable-rate mortgages rose to their highest levels since March.

title: Bundy brothers, 5 other Malheur wildlife refuge occupiers not guilty of conspiracy, firearm charges
text: Seven people involved in the anti-federal government occupation of the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge, including Ammon and Ryan Bundy, have been found not guilty of conspiring to impede federal workers from doing their jobs. A jury found all seven remaining occupiers not guilty of all charges except for one charge that has yet to be disclosed, KBOI reported. Ryan and Ammon Bundy, leaders of the six-week-long standoff in Oregon, and several other members were also found not guilty of possessing a firearm in a federal facility. A live video on the Bundy Ranch’s Facebook page showed some supporters claiming that Ammon Bundy’s attorney, Marcus Mumford, was tased in court by federal marshals. KATU reported that Mumford was in US Marshal custody after allegedly being tackled for shouting that Bundy was free to go after the verdict was announced. The Bundy brothers have not yet been released because of a federal hold relating to their standoff in Bunkerville, Nevada. According to KATU, Mumford’s insistence that they were to be released in Oregon led to the confrontation between him and federal marshals. “None of their conduct was directed at employees,” one defendant’s lawyer told KATU. He said there were no employees at the Malheur Reserve during the occupation and that no threats were made towards employees. Defendant Neil Wampler told KATU, “the verdict came back a clean sweep for all of us.” “This shows the absolute folly that has been committed by the federal government,” he said, and described the trial as “political prosecution.” The verdict was announced on Thursday, October 27, 2016.

title: Shock report: Facebook rejects women's code 35 percent more often!
text: Is Silicon Valley's sexism problem worse than we thought? A newly published report accuses Facebook of rejecting female developers’ code 35 percent more often than code written by men. The Wall Street Journal reports that a Facebook engineer gathered data last year showing that code written by women at the company was rejected more often than code written by male developers. The findings ignited a fierce debate inside Facebook over possible gender bias at the Silicon Valley giant. Even CEO Mark Zuckerberg was grilled about the report at a weekly town hall meeting. After the outcry, senior Facebook officials ran their own review of the engineer’s report. A month later, Facebook’s Head of Infrastructure, Jay Parikh, published an internal post blaming the rejection gap on the engineer’s rank and level of work – not gender. But did that settle anything? Many employees saw it as proof that female developers were not rising through the ranks of Google at the same rate as their male counterparts. A Facebook spokesperson told the Wall Street Journal that the original analysis by the Facebook engineer was “incomplete and inaccurate — performed by a former Facebook engineer with an incomplete data set.” Yet the spokesperson backed Mr. Parikh’s analysis – which was based on data unavailable to most employees. The spokesperson also admitted that there aren’t enough women at senior engineering levels at Facebook and across many Silicon Valley tech companies. Tracy Chou, a diversity advocate and former software engineer at Pinterest, warned: “especially for mass consumer products, there are just going to be blind spots.”

text: First ladies are the small group of women who occupy the East Wing of the White House while their husbands serve as presidents of the United States. Regarded as the true modern power brokers of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue, first ladies have taken different approaches to their public roles; some value the proximity to the country's top policy advisers, while others view the role as a prison term of teas, luncheons, dinners and photo opportunities. There are friendships among first ladies, as well as rivalries and relationships marked by hurt feelings and resentment, such as the one between Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama, Kate Andersen Brower writes in her new book, First Women, the Grace and Power of America's Modern First Ladies, published by Harper. The 2008 presidential campaign left deep and lasting damage in both the Clinton and the Obama camps, and it remains fresh. Michelle Obama, now 52, did not forget how Hillary Clinton mocked her husband's message of hope and change at a campaign rally in Ohio during that campaign. The sky will open, the light will come down, celestial choirs will be singing, and everyone will know that we should do the right thing, and the world would be perfect, Clinton said. The remarks begin at the 45-second mark of the video. Clinton's prediction was correct, as that did not happen, and she has remained bitter for years that Senator Ted Kennedy, her mentor in the Senate, did not support her presidential candidacy in 2008. A source in Clinton's inner circle told the author that Clinton, now 68, is running for president again out of vengeance for that loss.

title: Seth Meyers summarizes Monday's events
text: Monday, October 30, 2017 is a date of historical significance. On that day, former Trump campaign manager Paul Manafort and Manafort's top aide, Rick Gates, surrendered to the FBI and later entered not guilty pleas, while Trump foreign policy adviser George Papadopoulos pleaded guilty to lying to the FBI about his contacts with Russia, as a result of Robert Mueller's investigation into possible collusion between President Trump and that country. Events of this significance occur perhaps once every 15 or 20 years. When the news broke on Monday morning, it was expected that late-night television hosts would cover the story extensively. This was less because of the direct implications of Mueller's investigation than because of how the President and those linked to him would react. There was interest in what Trump would post on Twitter and how Fox News would cover the story, and both reacted as expected. The late-night hosts also covered the story. title: Tens of thousands march for and against Venezuela government
text: Tens of thousands of pro-government and anti-government protesters gathered on the streets of Venezuela's capital, Caracas. During Wednesday’s mass rallies, in which over 20 people were injured and 39 were detained, opponents accused President Nicolas Maduro of violating the constitutional order and blocking a recall referendum aimed at removing him from power. They also called for his immediate resignation. “This is a way of pressuring Maduro so he understands that he has to go,” said one protester. “Being passive is no use anymore. We have to apply more pressure,” another added. Meanwhile, large numbers of pro-government protesters gathered near the Miraflores presidential palace in support of Maduro. While the protests were taking place, the president held crisis security talks in response to the demonstrators’ demands. In a televised speech after the talks, he called for “political dialogue and peace in Venezuela.” Maduro has consistently cited Washington's role in his country’s political and economic problems and has accused the opposition of conspiring with the US against the South American country. “They are desperate, they have received the order from the north to destroy the Venezuelan revolution,” he added. On Tuesday, Maduro accused the opposition of attempting a “parliamentary coup” by voting to launch an impeachment process against him. “There has never been a parliamentary coup in Venezuela, and we shall not allow anything like this to happen, the right-wing here and there should know this,” Maduro said during a large rally by his supporters outside the presidential palace. The opposition-controlled National Assembly agreed earlier on Tuesday to begin the impeachment process against Maduro in response to the blocking of a bid to recall him last week.

title: Scandal-hit May lays down the law on harassment and bullying!
text: Westminster is in crisis – and Theresa May is scrambling. title: Obama orders review of Russian hacking, to be completed before he leaves office
text: President Obama has ordered a full review of Russian involvement in the hacking of the DNC and interference in the U.S. presidential election, and has asked for it to be completed before he leaves office. Lisa Monaco, Obama’s counterterrorism and homeland-security adviser, told reporters that it is incumbent upon the administration to take a deeper look into the situation. “We may have crossed into a new threshold, and it is incumbent upon us to take stock of that, to review, to conduct some after-action, to understand what has happened and to impart some lessons learned,” she said. She added that Obama wants the report completed before Donald Trump takes office on Jan. 20. The intelligence community attributed the hacking of the Democratic National Committee and other Democratic Party groups to Russia in October. Emails obtained in the hack, some of which appeared damaging to Hillary Clinton, were published on Wikileaks. A statement released by intelligence experts said the leaks were consistent with Russian tactics. “We believe, based on the scope and sensitivity of these efforts, that only Russia’s senior-most officials could have authorized these activities,” the statement said. title: Broke and beaten: French Socialists forced to sell historic HQ for $53 million!
text: How the mighty have fallen. France’s battered Socialist Party said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell its historic headquarters on the Paris Left Bank for 45.5 million euros ($53.89 million) – after a humiliating electoral defeat this year left it strapped for cash. The mansion has been in Socialist hands since 1980, just before Francois Mitterrand became the party’s first leader to win the presidency. Now it goes to French property developer Apsys. The collapse was brutal. The center-left party won just 29 parliamentary seats in a legislative election this year, down from 280 previously in the 577-strong chamber – costing it state subsidies. And that wasn't all. The Socialists were also crushed in the presidential race in May, as centrist newcomer Emmanuel Macron swept to power, blowing apart France’s traditional two-party system. The center-left party’s candidate limped into fifth place, after Francois Hollande – whose election five years earlier was hailed as a new dawn for French Socialists – did not seek re-election following an unpopular presidency. Is anyone surprised? Center-left parties across Europe have struggled to win back voters in the wake of recessions and a global banking crisis that have spawned newer political parties and boosted support in some cases for more radical forces on the left. Macron’s upstart Republic on the Move party now holds the largest number of seats in the lower house of parliament. Money from the sale of the Socialist headquarters will partly be used for future campaigns. The party said it would not have to move out until next September. The Socialists are currently run by a committee, and the party is due to hold a leadership contest next April.

title: Occupier David Fry released from jail: ‘I’m really free’
text: The last person to surrender in the takeover of the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge was released from prison hours after being acquitted on federal conspiracy charges on Thursday afternoon. David Fry was found not guilty of conspiring to impede workers from doing their jobs at the refuge through threats, intimidation or force. He was also acquitted of a firearms charge. The Ohio resident spoke to reporters before walking onto the streets of downtown Portland for the first time in 9 months. Fry said he looked forward to reuniting with family and friends to celebrate the verdict, and said that his effort to end corruption is not over. “It’s a wonderful feeling… to be acquitted by the highest authority in this country,” Fry said. “I definitely feel this was divine intervention playing in this.” “We’ve all got to work together and start making some changes because our governments worldwide aren’t for the people,” he said. “They’ve become the opposite.” He said guards at Multnomah County Jail treated him as if he were guilty, and that inmates are often not dealt with fairly or under the presumption of innocence. “I guess this is the greatest example of why you don’t treat people as guilty because they can be acquitted,” Fry said. Fry was one of the last 4 holdouts at the refuge and helped broadcast the final days of the standoff through YouTube livestreams. He allegedly threatened to commit suicide while on the phone with FBI crisis negotiators before he surrendered. Defense attorneys called his father, William Fry, to the witness stand to discuss his motives for joining the occupation. William said his son was “frustrated with corruption” and wanted to support Dwight and Steve Hammond, who he believed were falsely characterized as terrorists.

title: Inside Aleppo's hell: blood, grief and a fragile hope
text: On the edge of Aleppo’s ancient citadel, Zahra and her family were squatting in an apartment that now faces rebel lines. Plastic sheets covered its tall windows to hide the space from a sniper’s view as shelling boomed in the distance. Zahra, 25, who gave just one name, flicked between two photos on her phone. The first showed her husband, a Syrian Army soldier and the father of her unborn child. “Seven months,” she said, touching her belly. The second is heartbreaking. Her husband lay splayed on the ground, blood trickling from his nose, two other fallen soldiers beside him. He died two weeks ago. “May the men who did this also die,” she said with quiet determination. Four years of war have hardened hearts in Aleppo – a divided city and, for the past week, the scene of merciless fighting. A fragile truce brokered by the United States and Russia has crumbled in Syria, unleashing the worst violence in months. Russian fighter jets roar through the sky, pounding targets. The rebels fire barrages of mortar rounds and homemade missiles that crash into crowded neighborhoods. The war has inflamed sectarian tensions and turned into a proxy battle for regional and global interests. And who pays the price? Civilians. Most of the dead are civilians – at least 202 in the past week, in the eastern areas and on the west side, according to groups that monitor casualties. The violence shows a “monstrous disregard for civilian lives,” the United Nations’ human rights chief, Zeid Ra’ad, said Friday. One of the world’s oldest inhabited cities, Aleppo has for centuries been known as the crossroads of empires, with Ottoman, Armenian, Jewish and French influences.

title: Kremlin-backed billionaire caught in French tax probe!
text: A Russian billionaire is in deep trouble in France. A French judge on Wednesday placed Russian businessman and lawmaker Suleiman Kerimov – whose interests the Kremlin has vowed to defend – under formal investigation after his arrest in connection with a French tax evasion case, the prosecutor said. A second person was also put under formal investigation. A representative for Kerimov in the upper house of Russia’s parliament, where he sits as a lawmaker, declined to comment on the case on Wednesday. Polyus also declined to comment. Russia’s state-run Rossiya 24 TV station, citing an unnamed source, reported that Kerimov had denied any guilt.

Woodward is RIGHT! Hillary’s troubles are taking on the tones of Nixon’s DEMISE! And I should know – I was a young staffer in the Nixon White House, working in the West Wing before, during and after Watergate! The similarities are EERIE! In 1972, Richard Nixon was cruising to a landslide re-election – stunning foreign policy wins like the opening to China, arms control with the USSR and ending the Vietnam War, plus a good economy! Then it all came crashing down! The Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate office building was BROKEN INTO just before the election and files were stolen! The burglars were traced back to several mid-level people on Nixon’s OWN staff! Congress formed a Watergate committee! The Justice Department created a special prosecutor with subpoena powers! One by one my West Wing colleagues were dragged in to testify publicly before Congress and summoned behind closed doors by the special prosecutor! Every week, Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein had a NEW front-page bombshell in the Washington Post! Then came the BIGGEST shock: a secret Oval Office taping system recording the president’s meetings! The special prosecutor demanded the tapes. Nixon REFUSED!

title: Russia rigging the vote? Harry Reid sounds the alarm and demands F.B.I. probe!
text: Could Russia tamper with the November vote? Senate minority leader Harry Reid of Nevada thinks the danger is real. On Monday he asked the F.B.I. to investigate evidence suggesting that Russia may try to manipulate voting results in November. In a letter to F.B.I. director James B. Comey Jr., Mr. Reid warned that the threat of Russian interference “is more extensive than is widely known and may include the intent to falsify official election results.” Recent classified briefings from senior intelligence officials, Mr. Reid said in an interview, have left him fearful that President Vladimir V. Putin’s “goal is tampering with this election.” And the warning signs are already here. News reports on Monday said the F.B.I. warned state election officials several weeks ago that foreign hackers had exported voter registration data from computer systems in at least one state and had pierced the systems of a second. The bureau did not name the states, but Yahoo News, which first reported the confidential F.B.I. warning, said they were Arizona and Illinois. Matt Roberts, a spokesman for Arizona’s secretary of state, said the F.B.I. had told state officials that Russians were behind the Arizona attack. After the F.B.I. warning, Arizona pulled its voter registration database offline from June 28 to July 8 for a forensic exam of its systems, Mr. Roberts said. In its notice to states, the F.B.I. said the voter information had been “exfiltrated,” meaning it was shipped out of the state systems to another computer. That does not mean the data itself was tampered with. So what were the hackers after? It is unclear whether they intended to affect the election or wanted the data for other purposes, like gaining personal identifying information about voters.
